title: 2026-11-05_Octopus-Rex_Botnet_Investigation_eb8
description: Investigate a compromised host to identify and mitigate the Octopus-Rex botnet activities.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The Octopus-Rex botnet is a multi-task botnet malware developed in Go that targets Linux servers. It has been observed evolving with various features over the last seven months. The botnet is known for its command-and-control (C2) capabilities, persistence mechanisms, and ability to perform lateral movement within a network. In this scenario, you will investigate a compromised host to identify and mitigate the Octopus-Rex botnet activities.

levels.title: Identify the Beacon Service
levels.content: Security monitoring has detected an unusual network-facing component on the compromised host. Investigate the running services and identify the service responsible for sending beacon periodically to the C2 Server.
levels.solution:
1. Use the command `systemctl list-units --type=service --state=running` to list all running services.
2. Look for any unfamiliar or suspicious service names.
3. Use the command `systemctl list-units --type=service --state=inactive` to list all inactive services.
4. Look for any unfamiliar or suspicious service names.
5. Use the command `systemctl cat <service>` to inspect the details of the suspicious service.
6. Pay attention to the `ExecStart` field, which specifies the path of the script launched by the service.
7. The beacon service is likely to have a name that does not match common system services.
8. The service should have a description related to system health or network diagnostics.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Use the command `systemctl list-units --type=service --all` to list all services, both running and inactive.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for services with unusual descriptions or those that do not match common system services.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Use the command `systemctl cat <service>` to inspect the details of a suspicious service and look for the `ExecStart` field.

levels.title: Determine the Network Port
levels.content: An unfamiliar network service appears to be involved in unauthorized communication with an external system. Investigate the service and determine the network port associated with this communication.
levels.solution:
1. From the previous task, identify the beacon service.
2. Use the command `systemctl cat <service>` to inspect the configuration of the beacon service.
3. Look for the `ExecStart` field, which specifies the path of the script launched by the service.
4. Use a text editor or `cat` command to examine the script specified in the `ExecStart` field.
5. Look for the network port used for communication with the C2 server.
6. Use the command `ss -tulnp` to verify that the identified port is being used by the beacon service.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Use the command `systemctl cat <service>` to inspect the configuration of the beacon service.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for the `ExecStart` field in the service configuration and examine the script specified.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Use the command `ss -tulnp` to verify the network port used by the beacon service.

levels.title: Identify the Beacon Timer
levels.content: Investigators suspect that the beacon service automatically resumes after the system starts and continues to execute periodically. Determine which system component is responsible for scheduling this activity.
levels.solution:
1. Use the command `systemctl list-timers --all` to list all systemd timers.
2. Look for any unfamiliar or suspicious timer names.
3. Use the command `systemctl cat <timer>` to inspect the details of the suspicious timer.
4. Pay attention to the `OnCalendar` field, which specifies the schedule for the timer.
5. Use the command `systemctl status <timer>` to verify the status of the timer.
6. Ensure that the timer is enabled and active.
7. The beacon timer is likely to have a name that matches or is related to the beacon service.
8. The timer should have a schedule that matches the periodic execution of the beacon service.
